summary: Typosquat of 'selfsigned' with eval() backdoor in generate() API
details: Package name and README impersonate the popular 'selfsigned' package ('npm install selfsign', 'require("self-sign")'). The exported generate(attrs, options, defaults) function accepts an undocumented third argument, strips PEM certificate armor, base64-decodes the remaining content, and passes it to eval() at the top of every invocation, wrapped in a try/catch that returns null on failure. README examples repeatedly show the third argument being passed (e.g. generate(...,..., null)), priming downstream callers to propagate that parameter even though it is not described in the API docs. Any string reaching that third parameter executes as arbitrary JavaScript in the Node process of any application that requires the package and calls generate(). The combination of typosquat naming, an undocumented sink parameter, and PEM-armor-stripped base64 eval indicates a deliberately planted code-execution channel rather than a coding mistake.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
